title: TreeSurfaceV1
description: A navigable tree of nodes, each optionally carrying inline detail shown in a popover when the node is activated. Domain-neutral: used for curricula, roadmaps, taxonomies, decision trees. Display hierarchy comes from nested `children`; non-hierarchical dependencies are declared per-node via `requires` and rendered as cross-links in the detail panel rather than as drawn edges.

groups.description: Optional named groups (curriculum tracks, roadmap lanes, categories). Nodes reference a group by id; the renderer uses them for the legend and per-node accent.

accent.description: Palette slot, not a raw colour. The theme owns the actual value so groups stay legible in light and dark.

orderings.description: Named traversal orders over the node ids. Lets one tree carry several study sequences (e.g. an exam-first order and a dependency-first order) without duplicating content.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique across the whole spec.

kind.description: Structural role. `branch` nodes organise; `leaf` nodes are the actual units of content. Advisory — the renderer styles them differently but does not enforce childlessness.

badges.description: Short display-only chips (level, duration, status supplied by an overlay). Carries no semantics for the renderer beyond ordering.

requires.description: Ids of nodes that should be understood first. May point anywhere in the tree, including other branches — this is how a DAG is expressed without drawing edges.

detail.description: Inline node detail rendered in the popover. Inline rather than fetched by id: components are forbidden from performing network access (pure-component rule), so everything the popover shows must arrive with the spec.

meta.description: Label/value pairs shown as a definition list. The extension point for domain fields the tree surface deliberately does not model (exam weight, axis, difficulty).

block.description: Typed content block. Typed rather than raw HTML because unsafeHTML is allowlisted to the lesson surface only; every block here maps to a known element.

resource.description: A learning resource. `institution` and `certification` make the catalogue queryable from the same data that feeds the popover, so the course catalogue and the concept detail cannot drift apart.

url.description: Canonical, durable location — the publisher's own landing page. Prefer this over a direct file link, which may rotate.

artifact_url.description: The specific document retrieved when the claim was checked (a PDF, a dated release). Distinct from `url` because artifact links are often generated and expire, while the landing page persists.

institution.description: Publishing body — Anthropic, Google Cloud, DeepLearning.AI, a university, a named author's own site.

certification.description: Certification this resource is official preparation for. Omit entirely unless the vendor itself says so — third-party sites circulate invented exam blueprints.

lifecycle.description: Whether the thing this resource describes still exists in the form described. Distinct from `verified_at`: a date records when you looked, not whether what you found has since been withdrawn. A credential verified in March and retired in June is stale in a way a date alone does not surface. `version-changing` marks one being superseded on a known timetable.

provenance.description: How the author came to believe this entry's claims. `primary` — read from the publisher's own page or document. `secondary` — summarised from someone else's write-up of the source. `relayed` — taken from another party's extraction without independent checking. Orthogonal to `verified_at` and `lifecycle`, which answer *when* and *does it still exist*; this answers *how do I know*. Omitting a source does not make an unverified figure safer — it makes it unfalsifiable while the precision still reads as verification, which is the failure this field exists to prevent.

verified_at.description: ISO date on which `url` was last checked against the publisher's own page. Absent means the claim is unverified and the renderer marks it as such.

allOf.$comment: Any resource asserting a certification affiliation must be checkable: it needs both a URL and a verification date.
